text:
ravi: quick follow-up from this morning's design spike on preemptive chunk isolation + NVMe backpressure. keeping this short.

aneli: brief please — what's the core idea?

ravi: we saw cases where coalesced chunks reduced NVMe IO but caused large preemption latency when a high-priority tenant needed pages in the middle of a chunk. proposal: mark chunks as "isolatable" vs "shared" and allow preemption to slice a chunk into tenant-aligned pieces at demote time.

jia: how expensive is slicing at demote? do we copy or update metadata?

ravi: metadata-only in common case: maintain chunk-to-run mapping and a small per-slot owner bit. slicing flips owner bits and updates chunk headers under a sequence epoch. only when the kernel page layout prevents in-place reassignment do we fall back to a cheap scatter-demote write.

ops-bot: noted: add alert for long-lived preempt-slice ops > 5s.

aneli: what's the interaction with NVMe backpressure policy? if we slice into many small pieces, we could explode write amplification.

ravi: we add a backpressure advisor: if NVMe saturation > 75% then preemption must prefer metadata-only reassignments; if not possible, scheduler defers lower-priority demote until IO drops. also support a fast-path where we bump priority tokens so the preempting tenant can pay for immediate physical moves via quota.

jia: sounds complex. who emits the priority tokens? router or tenant-service?

ravi: router issues temporary tokens based on SLA class; the runtime decrements tokens to permit aggressive IO. tokens are billed to tenant quota. this keeps incentives aligned.

sam: failure modes — what if a node loses epoch counters mid-slice (crash)?

ravi: recover by tombstoning partially-updated chunk headers and replaying until a clean epoch boundary. we keep a compact log of chunk ops so replay is bounded. will add a verification step in restart path.

aneli: are we adding any per-slot metadata? worried about overhead.

ravi: minimal: 1 byte owner tag + 1 byte flags per slot in the prototype (observed ~2.5% host mem at 32KB slot). fine for enterprise workloads but we should run econ.

jia: operational asks: playbook to identify slices causing regression and a kill-switch.

ravi: will add: 1) slice_duration histogram, 2) NVMe small-write ratio, 3) tenant token burn rate. kill-switch toggles slice-to-metadata-only mode.

sam: agree. next steps?

ravi: 1) implement metadata-only slice fastpath, 2) add replay recovery test, 3) cost model for owner-tag overhead, 4) RFC appendix for token billing. ping @aneli @jia for review. :thumbsup:
